categories.label: Retail
categories.words: Up to ₹2 lakh. Most people apply here.
categories.odds_words: About 1 in 2 applicants gets one lot (an estimate, from 1.8x bids).
categories.note: Applying for more lots doesn't raise your chance: when retail is oversubscribed, each winner gets one lot.

categories.label: Small HNI (sHNI)
categories.words: More than ₹2 lakh, up to ₹10 lakh.
categories.odds_words: About 1 in 8 applicants gets the smallest application (an estimate, from 7.8x bids).

categories.label: Big HNI (bHNI)
categories.odds_words: About 1 in 14 applicants gets the smallest application (an estimate, from 14.5x bids).

odds_note: From the latest bids. They usually jump on the last day, so the odds will fall.

verdicts.track_record: A weak predictor of 1-year returns, about a coin flip: past IPOs with this verdict beat the Nifty 50 over 1 year 47% of the time (tested on 32 IPOs from 2024–25). Use it to understand the business, not to pick winners.

exits.title: Your listing-day rule
steps: Before Tue 3 Nov: decide your rule now, while you're calm, and write it in your journal.
On Tue 3 Nov, the shares start trading at 10 AM. Don't buy more on the first day's excitement.
If it opens above ₹330: you applied for a listing gain, so sell on listing day. Waiting for more turns a plan into a hope.
If it opens below ₹330: sell if it is more than 10% below your price, rather than holding on to wait for it to come back.

disclaimer: A learning aid worked out by fixed rules, not advice. Only apply with money you won't need soon, and decide for yourself.
